unit.title: Safe Process Boundaries: From Command Lines to Testable Interfaces
unit.audience: A student strong in algorithms who is developing production software-engineering habits
unit.scope: Design, implement, test, and document one small Python adapter that invokes a trusted local inspection tool without turning untrusted input into command syntax.
learning_objectives: Identify data, code, and trust boundaries in local process invocation.
Translate a security requirement into explicit interface invariants.
Use argument-vector process execution, a dedicated process group, bounded timeouts, captured output, and a controlled working directory.
Validate workspace-relative paths, including traversal and symlink cases.
Produce deterministic tests and durable evidence instead of relying on a prose claim of correctness.
required_outputs: A small Python implementation and trusted local helper fixture
Automated tests for normal, adversarial, failure, and timeout cases
A threat model and design decision record
Written responses to the comprehension prompts
scope_exclusions: Attacks against remote or third-party systems
Use of the catalog's unavailable individual challenges
A claim to cover any later CSE365 module

unit_complete_when: All required outputs exist and are attributable to the learner's attempt.
An examiner applies examiner_only/RUBRIC.md to the implementation, tests, evidence, and responses.
A worker-harness-controlled validator records a passing unit result.
completion_policy.course_completion_rule: This kickoff can never by itself complete the course. Later jobs must retrieve and classify usable official materials, construct additional bounded units, and validate each required unit before any course-level completion decision.
